topic: How Azure Durable Functions replay your orchestrator code
learn: Why an orchestrator body re-executes from line one, many times
How completed activities are answered from the event history
Why DateTime.Now and Guid.NewGuid break a Durable Function

faq.q: Why does a Durable Functions orchestrator run from the top every time?
faq.a: The orchestrator replays its entire function body from line one on every checkpoint, but activities that already completed answer instantly from the recorded event history instead of running again — that's how it resumes exactly where it left off without keeping the process alive between awaits.

faq.q: Why do DateTime.Now and Guid.NewGuid break a Durable Function?
faq.a: Replay re-executes the same code path multiple times, so any non-deterministic call would return a different value on each replay and desynchronize the orchestrator from its own history. Use the context's deterministic equivalents instead.

stages.title: It did not run once
stages.desc: Your orchestrator function body executes again and again from the top — the Functions runtime, not a bug, and you only see the final result.
stages.js:
MSD.after(80, function(){ MSD.cls('#t-hook', 'on', true); MSD.punch('#t-hook-big'); });
      MSD.after(900, function(){ MSD.punch('#t-hook-big', 4); });

stages.title: It looks like normal code
stages.desc: Three sequential awaits, top to bottom, reading like ordinary C#. Nothing in the syntax hints that the whole function replays.

stages.title: It stops at the first await
stages.desc: The runtime schedules the activity function on the task hub, then the orchestrator exits completely — no thread sits blocked waiting.

stages.title: The result lands in history
stages.desc: When the activity finishes, its output is appended as an event to the orchestration's history table in Azure Storage.

stages.title: Then it runs again
stages.desc: From line one, on a new thread. This time the first await returns instantly from history instead of calling the activity again.

stages.title: One step deeper each time
stages.desc: Every completed activity extends the history table by one event, so each replay gets exactly one step further before hitting new work.

stages.title: This is why DateTime breaks
stages.desc: DateTime.Now, Guid.NewGuid, random — anything non-deterministic returns a new value on every replay, so execution stops matching history.

stages.title: Keep the replay invisible
stages.desc: Use context.CurrentUtcDateTime and context.NewGuid instead — deterministic replacements that keep the whole replay mechanism invisible.

end.title: Your orchestrator is a replay engine
end.sub: The code reads top to bottom. Underneath, it re-runs from line one until every await has an answer.

post.caption:
Azure Durable Functions do not run your orchestrator once.

They run it from the top again after every activity, replaying completed steps from an event history — which is exactly why DateTime.UtcNow quietly breaks it.

Did you know your orchestrator code re-executes?
